title: Customs Clearance Verification and Approval Procedures
summary: This thread tracks the evolution of administrative verification and approval protocols for customs clearance. It shifts from manual inter-departmental communication and physical document submission to digital verification, risk-based management, and automated system-driven clearance.

evolution.verification_method: From manual communication to digital system validation to automated risk-based selectivity.
evolution.institutional_involvement: Increased integration between Customs, VAT, and Intelligence units.

timeline.change: Introduced manual verification via phone/email between customs and VAT officials.
Transitioned to digital verification using Customs/VAT online systems and website-based BIN validation.
Streamlined the verification requirement to focus on compliance with specific clauses and formal approval by DC/AC level officers.
Shifted to an automated risk management system (ARMS) using selectivity criteria (Red/Yellow/Blue/Green lanes) for clearance.

member_objects.resolved_text: (৫) শুল্কায়ন তত্ত্বাবধানকারী সংশ্লিষ্ট ডেপুটি কমিশনার বা সহকারী কমিশনার শুল্কায়নে বিলম্ব পরিহারের লক্ষ্যে ফোন, ফ্যাক্স বা ই-মেইলে সংশ্লিষ্ট মূসক এলাকার ডেপুটি কমিশনার বা সহকারী কমিশনারগণের সহিত যোগাযোগ করিয়া ১, ২ ও ৩ নং শর্তের তথ্য ও সঠিকতা যাচাই করিয়া লইবেন।

Customs Clearance: The customs official overseeing the assessment process is mandated to communicate with their counterparts in the relevant Value Added Tax area to verify information and ensure the accuracy of conditions related to the shipment.
This administrative measure is implemented specifically to prevent unnecessary delays during the customs clearance process.
Deputy Commissioner of Customs: The Deputy Commissioner is tasked with coordinating with the corresponding Value Added Tax authorities via digital or telephonic means to facilitate the verification of documentation and conditions.
Assistant Commissioner of Customs: The Assistant Commissioner is authorized to liaise with the relevant Value Added Tax officials to confirm the accuracy of specific regulatory conditions, thereby ensuring operational efficiency.
Value Added Tax: The respective authorities managing Value Added Tax are required to cooperate with customs officials to verify data and conditions to expedite the customs assessment procedure.

Customs Clearance: The appropriate officer must verify compliance with all established conditions regarding the import and customs clearance process.
Customs clearance must be approved by the relevant Deputy Commissioner or Assistant Commissioner.
Business Identification Number: Customs officials must verify the authenticity of the Business Identification Number using authorized customs or VAT online systems and official government websites to avoid processing delays.
National Board of Revenue: The official website of the National Board of Revenue is designated as a source for verifying taxpayer registration information during the customs clearance process.
Customs Computerised Entry Processing Sy: This system is used by customs officials to verify taxpayer information and ensure regulatory compliance during the import process.
Value Added Tax Commissionerate: The website of the VAT Commissionerate is an authorized portal for the verification of taxpayer registration documents.
Importation of Goods: Details of every consignment cleared under this notification must be formally communicated to the relevant VAT authorities.
Importers are required to provide a formal undertaking stating that the imported raw materials or components will be utilized specifically for the manufacturing of air conditioners.

member_objects.clause_title: আমদানি ও শুল্কায়ন সংক্রান্ত অন্যান্য বিষয়সহ
member_objects.resolved_text: ২। আমদানি ও শুল্কায়ন সংক্রান্ত অন্যান্য বিষয়সহ দফা (১) ও (২) এ উল্লিখিত শর্ত পরিপালন করা হইয়াছে কিনা তাহা সংশ্লিষ্ট শুল্কায়নকারী কর্মকর্তা কর্তৃক যাচাই করিয়া নিশ্চিত হইতে হইবে এবং শুল্কায়ন তত্ত্বাবধানকারী সংশ্লিষ্ট ডেপুটি কমিশনার বা সহকারী কমিশনার পর্যায়ে শুল্কায়ন অনুমোদন করাইতে হইবে।

Customs Clearance: The customs official must verify that all specified import and customs-related conditions are met before proceeding with clearance. This process ensures that compliance requirements are strictly followed prior to the approval of any importation.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The officer responsible for customs clearance is mandated to perform a thorough verification of the conditions associated with the import, ensuring compliance with relevant legal provisions.
Deputy Commissioner of Customs: The Deputy Commissioner or the Assistant Commissioner is responsible for the final supervision and approval of the customs clearance process, ensuring that the verification conducted by the customs official is correct.
Assistant Commissioner of Customs: The Assistant Commissioner is authorized to oversee and grant the necessary approval for customs clearance, providing a supervisory layer to ensure that all procedural and import conditions are satisfied.

member_objects.clause_title: কাস্টমস রিস্ক ম্যানেজমেন্ট কমিশনারেট ব্যতীত বোর্ডের অন্যান্য দপ্তর কর্তৃক ঝুঁকি ব্যবস্থাপনা পদ্ধতি
member_objects.resolved_text:
৪। কাস্টমস রিস্ক ম্যানেজমেন্ট কমিশনারেট ব্যতীত বোর্ডের অন্যান্য দপ্তর কর্তৃক ঝুঁকি ব্যবস্থাপনা পদ্ধতি।—(১) বোর্ডের অধীন কাস্টমস স্টেশন, মূসক কমিশনারেট, কাস্টমস গোয়েন্দা ও তদন্ত অধিদপ্তর, সেন্ট্রাল ইন্টেলিজেন্স সেল, কাস্টমস বন্ড কমিশনারেটসমূহ কোনো পণ্যচালানের বিষয়ে শুল্কায়নের পূর্বে ঝুঁকি সংক্রান্ত আগাম তথ্য প্রাপ্ত হইলে উহা এআরএমএস সফটওয়্যারে এন্ট্রি করিবে।
(২) পণ্যচালানের শুল্কায়ন সম্পন্ন হইবার পর উপ-বিধি (১) এ বর্ণিত কোনো তথ্য প্রাপ্ত হইলে সংশ্লিষ্ট কাস্টমস স্টেশন বা কাস্টমস গোয়েন্দা ও তদন্ত অধিদপ্তর বা সেন্ট্রাল ইন্টেলিজেন্স সেল তাৎক্ষণিকভাবে প্রতিরোধমূলক প্রয়োজনীয় ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণ করিবে এবং উক্ত ব্যবস্থার ফলাফল এআরএমএস সফটওয়্যারে এন্ট্রি করিবে।
(৩) যাত্রী সংশ্লিষ্ট ঝুঁকি সংক্রান্ত কোনো তথ্য প্রাপ্ত হইলে সংশ্লিষ্ট কাস্টমস স্টেশন বা কাস্টমস গোয়েন্দা ও তদন্ত অধিদপ্তর বা সেন্ট্রাল ইন্টেলিজেন্স সেল তাৎক্ষণিকভাবে প্রতিরোধমূলক প্রয়োজনীয় সকল ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণ করিবে এবং উক্ত ব্যবস্থার ফলাফল এআরএমএস সফটওয়্যারে এন্ট্রি করিবে।

National Board of Revenue: The Board oversees various departments that are responsible for implementing risk management procedures regarding customs consignments and passengers.
ARMS Software: This software serves as the central platform for recording risk-related information for cargo consignments and the outcomes of preventive actions taken by customs offices.
Customs offices and investigation units must input the results of any preventive measures taken regarding cargo or passengers directly into the ARMS software.
Customs Risk Management: Various customs departments, including customs stations, VAT commissionerates, intelligence cells, and bonding commissionerates, must document pre-clearance risk information in the designated system.
Upon identifying risk-related information after the customs clearance process for goods, the relevant departments are mandated to take immediate preventive actions and update the system accordingly.

In cases where risk-related information concerning passengers is discovered, the authorized customs departments must execute immediate preventive measures and record the results in the risk management software.
Customs Station: These stations are tasked with inputting advance risk information into the risk management software and carrying out preventive measures for both goods and passengers when necessary.
Customs Intelligence and Investigation D: This directorate is responsible for entering risk data into the software and initiating preventive actions against identified risks related to goods or passengers.
Central Intelligence Cell: The cell is required to record risk information regarding cargo and passengers in the risk management software and implement necessary preventive steps when such risks are identified.
Customs Commissioner: This office is mandated to input advance risk information concerning cargo consignments into the designated customs risk management system.
Value Added Tax Commissionerate: This department is responsible for recording advance risk information related to cargo consignments into the authorized risk management system.

Automated System for Customs Data: The system uses selectivities to determine processing channels for cargo and passengers. It establishes an automated risk management framework to evaluate shipment risks based on pre-defined indicators.

The system classifies consignments into red, yellow, blue, and green lanes, and passengers into red and green channels for customs clearance. It also assigns risk scores based on the degree of similarity to established risk indicators.

It creates profiles for importers, exporters, agents, and passengers to identify potential risks through data processing. The system incorporates historical records, intelligence data, and advanced analytical methods to refine its risk assessment indicators.
Data Analytics: Advanced data analytics, machine learning, and artificial intelligence are utilized to process customs documentation and records. These methodologies serve as the technical foundation for identifying and setting risk indicators within the automated management framework.
Manifest Data: Consignment information and related data are compared against established risk indicators to determine potential security or compliance threats during the customs clearance process.
